newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended higher, recovering from lows after release of U.S. economic data which were seen as favourable for U.S. Treasuries.
The U.S. fourth quarter employment cost index showed a 0.8 percent rise, slightly below the 0.9 percent rise forecast.

"There was some selling this morning, mainly marking down the prices before the big figure. We managed to get prices down to technical levels, but volume was pretty low. After the release of the figures, I think there was a lot of short-covering," one Swiss-based trader said.
The trader said the Swiss market was mainly Treasury-driven. Domestic factors offered little in the way of new direction.

J.P. Morgan launched a 150 million Swiss franc bond Tuesday morning. The issue, for four years and 10 months, with a 2.00 percent coupon priced at 97.30, was quoted by lead manager SBC Warburg yielding 3.02 percent in late trade.
One trader said the swap window for five- to six-year maturities was still open, and further issues were possible in that spectrum.
March Comi medium-term bond down seven at 111.10
Mar Euro Swiss francs up three at 98.19.
